# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_017_page_001.jpg

---

17:1 For great are your judgments, and hard to tell; therefore undisciplined souls went astray.

17:2 For when lawless men supposed that they held the holy nation in their power, they themselves lay bound with fetters of darkness and long night, shut up under their roofs, exiles from eternal providence.

17:3 For thinking to remain hidden in their secret sins, they were scattered under a dark veil of forgetfulness, terribly frightened, and troubled by apparitions.

17:4 For not even the inner chamber that held them protected them from fear; but crashing sounds full of dread rang around them, and gloomy phantoms with sullen faces appeared.

17:5 And no force of fire was strong enough to give light, nor were the brilliant flames of the stars able to illuminate that dreadful night.

17:6 Only an automatic fire shone through to them, full of dread; and in terror they deemed the things they saw to be worse than that sight which was not seen.

17:7 The mockeries of their magic art were brought low, and their boasted wisdom was a reproach.

17:8 For those who promised to drive away fears and disorders from a sick soul, themselves were sick with a ridiculous fear.

17:9 For even if nothing frightening disturbed them, frightened by the passing of beasts and the hissing of serpents,

17:10 they perished trembling, refusing to see even the air, which could not be escaped on any side.

17:11 For wickedness is a coward, condemned by its own testimony; and when pressed by conscience, it always magnifies misfortunes.

17:12 For fear is nothing other than a surrender of the resources that come from reason;

17:13 and the expectation from within, being less, counts the ignorance more than the cause of the torment.

17:14 But they, throughout that night which was powerless — and which came upon them from the recesses of powerless Hades — sleeping the same sleep,

17:15 now were driven by monstrous apparitions, now were paralyzed by their soul's surrender; for sudden fear came upon them and unexpected.

17:16 Then if any one of them fell down, he was kept under guard, shut up in a prison not made of iron;

17:17 for whether he was a farmer or a shepherd or a worker at tasks in the wilderness, he was overtaken, and endured the inescapable fate; for they were all bound by the same chain of darkness.

17:18 Whether it was a whistling wind, or a melodious sound of birds among the spreading branches, or a rhythm of rushing water,

17:19 or a harsh crash of rocks hurled down, or the unseen running of leaping animals, or the sound of savage roaring beasts, or an echo reverberating from a hollow mountain — these things paralyzed them with terror.

17:20 For the whole world was illuminated with brilliant light and conducted its work unhindered;

17:21 while over those people alone heavy night was spread, an image of the darkness that was to receive them; but they were to themselves more burdensome than the darkness.
